Mantener unidas estas gigantescas organizaciones deportivas; no son partidos políticos. Esto será un territorio desconocido", comentó. INFANTINO SE RECUPERA Hay otra razón por la que la atención se está desplazando hacia la convivencia con Infantino en lugar de su sustitución: su posición parece haberse fortalecido desde que estalló la crisis. El presidente de una federación nacional, que habló con Reuters bajo condición de anonimato, cree que los opositores de Infantino dejaron pasar su mejor oportunidad cuando la reacción negativa estaba en su punto álgido y que ahora está recuperando apoyos de cara a las elecciones de marzo. El presidente de la FIFA tendrá una sucesión de oportunidades en los próximos meses para reunirse con los dirigentes de las federaciones nacionales en torneos, congresos y eventos de las confederaciones, incluidas varias reuniones en África. El presidente de la federación espera que Infantino aproveche esas reuniones para mantener el apoyo entre los dirigentes del fútbol de cara a las elecciones presidenciales de la FIFA de marzo de 2027. La importancia política de las federaciones más pequeñas también quedó patente en una propuesta de Ceferin y del presidente de la Concacaf, Víctor Montagliani, para que la FIFA distribuya al menos 10 millones de dólares de sus reservas a cada una de sus 211 federaciones miembro durante el próximo ejercicio financiero. Para muchas federaciones que dependen en gran medida de la financiación de la FIFA, estas sumas podrían suponer un cambio radical. Si Infantino resulta reelegido, el presidente de la asociación cree que algunas federaciones que se han opuesto a él podrían acabar mostrándose menos hostiles, al llegar a la conclusión de que hay poco que ganar con cuatro años de confrontación permanente. Esa posibilidad significa que una "guerra fría" no es inevitable.

item.title: Japan schoolboy Ohashi shrugs off COVID to smash 200m breaststroke world record
item.description: Little more than a week after coming down with COVID-19, 17-year-old schoolboy Shin Ohashi lit up the Asian Games pool with a breaststroke world record that left Japan wondering whether a successor to Kosuke Kitajima had emerged.
item.dc:creator: Ian Ransom
item.content:encoded: Little more than a week after coming down with COVID-19, 17-year-old schoolboy Shin Ohashi lit up the Asian Games pool with a breaststroke world record that left Japan wondering whether a successor to Kosuke Kitajima had emerged. Ohashi stormed to his second gold of the Games with a time of 2:04.83 in the 200m event at the Tokyo Aquatics Centre, smashing the previous record (2:05.48) set by China's Qin Haiyang at the 2023 world championships in Fukuoka. Big things were expected of Ohashi at this meet, having won five medals at last year's world junior championships. Falling ill in the leadup was not ideal but he said being forced to take some rest may have helped him. "Regarding COVID, after all, there was a part where it created a little anxiety for me mentally," said Ohashi, who shared the 100m breaststroke gold with China's Dong Zhihao three days ago, with Qin taking bronze. "But, conversely, physically it was very -- well, in a sense, I think it was good that I was able to properly rest my body as a period of recovery." Olympic champion Leon Marchand, who visited the Games pool this week, described Ohashi as a "scary" prospect ahead of the Frenchman's defence of his 200m breaststroke title at Los Angeles 2028. NATURAL MUSCLE His coach Shin Ota said he was a great learner, even if like many high school boys, he was often glued to his phone. "He has this kind of absent-minded appearance, and looks as though he's not thinking about anything, but, yeah, he really loves swimming and he's incredibly enthusiastic about studying it," said Ota, admitting the world record was a surprise to him. "I've answered this in various interviews, but I have this sense that I hardly teach him anything. "But, as you can see, he's got a lot of muscle, but it's not as though he's doing weight training. It's natural muscle, so I think that's another part of what's remarkable about him." Japan has a proud history in the breaststroke, and counts Kitajima as one of the nation's swimming greats. Kitajima claimed back-to-back 100 and 200m breaststroke gold medals at the 2004-08 Olympics, the only swimmer to achieve that "double-double". Ohashi's coach said it was early days for Ohashi but he could see him following Kitajima onto an Olympic podium. "While gaining those experiences one by one and getting accustomed to them, I think he'll surely be able to win a medal at the Olympics as well," said Ota. "And for him to become like Kitajima, he'll also need to grow as a person."

item.title: Brewers eye elusive century mark in series finale vs. Phillies
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers have never won 100 games in a season, but they have a chance to reach that milestone Thursday when they conclude their road series with the Philadelphia Phillies.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Milwaukee Brewers have never won 100 games in a season, but they have a chance to reach that milestone Thursday when they conclude their road series with the Philadelphia Phillies. After losing 6-4 in Tuesday's series opener, Milwaukee (99-59) evened things up with a 4-1 triumph on Wednesday. The Brewers' 11th win in 14 games put them on the precipice of the century mark with four games left in the regular season. Logan Henderson allowed just one run over five innings in his final tune-up before the postseason. He'll follow Jacob Misiorowski in the playoffs, giving Milwaukee a formidable 1-2 punch. "He's been fantastic for us. Unsung hero, for sure," Milwaukee manager Pat Murphy said of Henderson. "Miz getting all the attention, but this kid has matched him in a lot of ways, just his consistency and getting outs." The Brewers already have clinched a first-round bye, although they are hoping to finish ahead of the Los Angeles Dodgers (97-61) for the best record in the majors and home-field advantage throughout the postseason. The Phillies (87-71), meanwhile, entered Wednesday with a magic number of two to secure a postseason berth. However, they didn't do their part against Milwaukee as Aaron Nola gave up home runs to Brice Turang and Christian Yelich while the offense went 0-for-12 with runners in scoring position. "It's always frustrating," Philadelphia interim manager Don Mattingly said. "Everybody wants to get a hit in those spots. ... You feel like if you can get a run here and a run there, it really changes the game." The Phillies will look to bounce back behind rookie right-hander Andrew Painter (3-10, 5.59 ERA), who is winless in his past five starts. He absorbed a 10-3 loss to the New York Mets in his last outing, as he gave up four runs in 5 1/3 innings, allowing a pair of home runs in the process. "I don't worry about Paint's toughness, honestly," Mattingly said. "(I see him) bouncing back and continuing to make pitches. I don't worry about Paint from the standpoint of growth, handling situations." Painter was the bulk innings pitcher against the Brewers on June 12 and yielded five runs in five innings in a 6-0 defeat. He did not take the loss. Right-hander Bryse Wilson (0-0, 3.67) will make his first start of the season after appearing in 15 games out of the bullpen for three teams. He made one appearance for the Phillies on June 18 and then saw action in two games for the Chicago Cubs before joining the Brewers. Wilson, who has a 2.55 ERA in 12 appearances for Milwaukee, has been out since late August with a back injury. He knows his job generally is to eat innings, particularly with the Brewers looking to keep their pitching staff healthy and rested with the postseason right around the corner. "If I come in and we're down a lot of runs, I know that innings have to be covered," Wilson said recently. "I just go in and do the best I can to cover as many innings to where the next day, we have a much better chance to win because everybody's available and there's more options to go to in the bullpen." Wilson has appeared in five career games (three starts) against the Phillies, going 1-2 with a 6.35 ERA. --Field Level Media

item.title: UE mantiene contactos de alto nivel con EEUU por supuesto plan de prohibir exportación de diésel: portavoz
item.description: Un portavoz de la Comisión Europea dijo el jueves que se están manteniendo contactos de alto nivel entre la Unión Europea y Estados Unidos en medio de los rumores sobre un plan estadounidense para prohibir las exportaciones de gasóleo, algo que, según la UE, podría tener un impacto negativo para ambas partes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Un portavoz de la Comisión Europea dijo el jueves que se están manteniendo contactos de alto nivel entre la Unión Europea y Estados Unidos en medio de los rumores sobre un plan estadounidense para prohibir las exportaciones de gasóleo, algo que, según la UE, podría tener un impacto negativo para ambas partes. Politico informó de que Washington está preparando una prohibición de 90 días a las exportaciones de gasóleo ante el repunte de los precios previo a las elecciones de mitad de mandato de noviembre, aunque el secretario de Energía estadounidense, Chris Wright, lo desmintió. "Se están manteniendo contactos de alto nivel entre la Unión Europea y la Administración estadounidense. Esperamos que unos socios cercanos se consulten mutuamente antes de adoptar medidas que afecten a los mercados comunes", declaró Olof Gill a los periodistas. Los analistas han señalado que una prohibición de las exportaciones de gasóleo por parte de Estados Unidos contribuiría poco a aliviar los precios en ese país, pero que incluso una prohibición parcial podría provocar escasez de producto en Europa y en otros lugares. El gasóleo es el combustible que impulsa el transporte, la maquinaria agrícola y otros equipos utilizados para producir y transportar mercancías, y el aumento de los precios del combustible aviva la inflación al encarecer el costo de todo, desde los productos alimenticios hasta los materiales industriales. Los precios del gasóleo se han disparado debido a los bajos niveles de existencias y a las perturbaciones causadas por las guerras en Ucrania y Oriente Medio. Rusia, el segundo mayor exportador mundial tras Estados unidos, prohibió las exportaciones de gasóleo en julio hasta finales de septiembre. Una prohibición de las exportaciones por parte de Washington obligaría a las refinerías estadounidenses a recortar la cantidad de crudo que procesan, lo que a su vez reduciría la producción de gasolina y otros productos y haría subir los precios de esos combustibles, según han señalado analistas y operadores. La UE es importadora neta de gasóleo y tendría que competir con compradores de América Latina, África y Asia por un volumen menor de suministros disponibles.

item.title: Tivit investirá R$1 bi em aquisições na América Latina
item.description: A companhia brasileira de tecnologia Tivit anunciou nesta quinta-feira um programa de R$1 bilhão em aquisições na América Latina, em estratégia para ampliar portfólio de tecnologias proprietárias e criar plataformas especializadas em setores estratégicos.
item.dc:creator: Igor Sodre
item.content:encoded: A companhia brasileira de tecnologia Tivit anunciou nesta quinta-feira um programa de R$1 bilhão em aquisições na América Latina, em estratégia para ampliar portfólio de tecnologias proprietárias e criar plataformas especializadas em setores estratégicos. O programa priorizará a aquisição de companhias desenvolvedoras de software e hardware proprietários com faturamento entre R$20 milhões e R$200 milhões por ano. Não há prazo preestabelecido para desembolso dos recursos. A Tivit foi adquirida no ano passado pelo grupo italiano Almaviva. "Ficamos um ano nessa jornada de integração e agora estamos mais maduros. Então esse momento acaba abrindo espaço para um investimento mais agressivo", disse Mitri Brito, diretor de estratégia, fusões e aquisições e marketing da Tivit. Segundo o executivo, o investimento de R$1 bilhão será financiado por meio da geração própria de caixa da Tivit, conforme as novas aquisições forem concretizadas. "Vemos oportunidades no nosso mercado", acrescentou Brito. Os investimentos estão organizados em seis plataformas verticais, sendo elas: Governo, com foco em Segurança Pública e Defesa, Mercado Financeiro, Transportes, Manufatura, Saúde e 'Utilities', além de duas plataformas horizontais, Inteligência Artificial e Segurança Cibernética. Para executar o programa, a companhia desenvolveu estudos dedicados por indústria, analisando necessidades dos clientes, dinâmica competitiva, tendências tecnológicas e oportunidades de inovação. "Durante o estudo, nós observamos oportunidades de tecnologia, mas também percebemos dores verticais, específicas de cada indústria. Para resolver isso, a avaliação foi de que precisávamos tanto de uma abordagem horizontal quanto vertical", disse Brito. A Tivit mapeou 620 empresas que poderiam ser alvos de aquisição. Dessas, 308 foram selecionadas e abordadas. No fim, a Tivit realizou conversas com 75 potenciais alvos e mantém 15 oportunidades em fase de aprofundamento de negocição. O executivo disse que as empresas que ficaram de fora do programa foram filtradas por motivos distintos, como desalinhamento de interesse por parte dos fundadores, falta de maturidade comercial ou modelos de negócios não escaláveis, enquanto as 15 finalistas avançaram por meio de análises qualitativas de potencial de escala. "Olhamos com muito bons olhos a IA. Temos serviços e produtos no portfólio tanto para (segmentos) horizontais quanto para verticais", disse o executivo. O grupo Almaviva destinou mais de R$6 bilhões a operações de fusão e aquisição nos últimos dois anos, sendo aproximadamente metade desse montante foi direcionado à América Latina. Além da Tivit, o grupo ampliou sua presença em diferentes mercados por meio de aquisições como a Iteris, especializada em mobilidade inteligente nos Estados Unidos; Mabrian, voltada a tecnologias para turismo; e a B.M. Tecnologie Industriali, especializada em soluções para saneamento e gestão de água.

item.title: Canada July retail sales fall 0.7%; seen up 1.3% in August
item.description: Canadian monthly retail sales fell by 0.7% in July, marginally better than an average of analysts' expectations, primarily led by declines at general merchandise retailers, data showed on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Promit Mukherjee
item.content:encoded: Canadian monthly retail sales fell by 0.7% in July, marginally better than an average of analysts' expectations, primarily led by declines at general merchandise retailers, data showed on Thursday. Retail sales, which include purchases of cars, furniture, food and gasoline, are considered an early indicator of gross domestic product growth and account for about 40% of consumer spending. Retail sales dropped to C$73.70 billion ($52.25 billion) in July from C$74.25 billion in the prior month, Statistics Canada said. However, sales are likely to rebound once again in August and increase by 1.3%, the statistics agency said in an advance estimate. Sales were down in eight of nine sub-sectors in July. In volume terms, retail sales decreased 1.1%. General merchandise retailers, stores that sell a broad mix of unrelated goods from groceries to food and apparel to electronics, posted the biggest decline in sales in July. This category, which contributes up to 15% of total retail sales, slumped by 1.9%. Sales at motor vehicles and parts dealers, which account for the biggest share of retail sales, dropped by 0.8%, data showed. Purchases at food and beverage retailers, the second-biggest category, dropped 0.1%; however, sales at supermarket and grocery retailers hardly changed. The category of building materials was the only sub-sector which posted an increase, with sales increasing 0.8%. "We don't expect the momentum to extend, as lingering trade uncertainty will likely weigh on discretionary spending ahead," Katherine Judge, senior economist at CIBC Capital Markets, wrote in a note. This means the Bank of Canada will not be raising rates in the near term, she added. ($1=$1.4105 Canadian)

item.title: Acea si aggiudica gara in Perù per trattamento acque reflue a Lima
item.description: Acea si è aggiudicata una gara in Perù per il trattamento delle acque reflue a Lima del valore di 4,5 milioni di dollari.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Acea (ACE.MI) si è aggiudicata una gara in Perù per il trattamento delle acque reflue a Lima del valore di 4,5 milioni di dollari. "Acea Perù si aggiudica la gestione e manutenzione di 8 impianti di depurazione nella zona Sud di Lima" si legge in un comunicato, in cui si precisa che si tratta "del quarto contratto negli ultimi due anni per un valore complessivo di 145 milioni di euro". Acea serve circa 10 milioni di abitanti in America Latina nel settore idrico, con un impegno di oltre 1400 dipendenti concentrato prevalentemente in Perù, Honduras e Repubblica Dominicana.

item.title: Morgan Stanley Asia deals leaked in missent email attachment
item.description: A senior Morgan Stanley banker covering financial sponsors in Asia accidentally leaked their deal pipeline in an email sent to clients, according to six people with knowledge of the matter.
item.dc:creator: Kane Wu, Julie Zhu
item.content:encoded: A senior Morgan Stanley (MS.N) banker covering financial sponsors in Asia accidentally leaked their deal pipeline in an email sent to clients, according to six people with knowledge of the matter. The banker attached the financial sponsors group's deal pipeline by mistake in a weekly update email he sent to clients, the people said. "Morgan Stanley takes client confidentiality extremely seriously. We promptly took steps to address this inadvertent sharing of information and we continue to engage with relevant parties," a spokesperson for the Wall Street bank said in an emailed response to Reuters on Thursday. The banker later retracted the email and apologised for the mishap, urging recipients to delete copies of the attachment and refrain from circulating the document, according to a screenshot of the email seen by Reuters. The list, dated September 21, contained about 60 live IPO, M&A and block trade deals across Greater China, South Korea, Southeast Asia, India and the EMEA region. It also included over 50 deals that were categorised as "pitching" and nearly 30 deals categorised as "on hold". All of those deals concern Asian companies. The vast majority of the companies on the list are portfolios of major global and regional private equity and venture capital firms. Bloomberg first reported on the incident late on Wednesday. The list did not contain details of any of the deals, and a lot of them have already been reported, according to some people who received the email.

item.title: Wall Street abre em baixa com alta do petróleo por incerteza com Oriente Médio
item.description: Os principais índices de ações de Wall Street abriram em baixa nesta quinta-feira enquanto as tensões no Oriente Médio impulsionavam os preços do petróleo e os rendimentos dos Treasuries.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os principais índices de ações de Wall Street abriram em baixa nesta quinta-feira enquanto as tensões no Oriente Médio impulsionavam os preços do petróleo e os rendimentos dos Treasuries. Os investidores também demonstravam cautela antes da cúpula entre os presidentes dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, e da China, Xi Jinping. O Índice Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) caía 0,19% na abertura, para 51.415,75 pontos. O S&P 500 (.SPX) recuava 0,51%, a 7.666,99 pontos, enquanto o Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) tinha queda de 0,75%, para 26.734,508 pontos. (Reportagem de Johann M Cherian em Bengaluru)

item.title: STICHWORT Ausländische Unternehmen auf Einkaufstour in Deutschland
item.description: Deutsche Unternehmen bleiben im Ausland begehrt. 107 Milliarden Dollar zahlten ausländische Konzerne und Investoren in den ersten neun Monaten 2026 für Firmen aus Deutschland, doppelt so viel wie ein Jahr zuvor, wie aus den am Donnerstag veröffentlichten "League Tables" des Londoner Börsenbetreibers und Finanzdatenanbieters LSEG hervorgeht. Auf ihr Konto gehen damit fast 60 Prozent des gesamten Volumens von Fusionen und Übernahmen mit deutscher Beteiligung von 179,3 Milliarden Dollar (Stand: 23. September). Bei fünf der sechs größten Deals kam der Käufer aus dem Ausland.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Deutsche Unternehmen bleiben im Ausland begehrt. 107 Milliarden Dollar zahlten ausländische Konzerne und Investoren in den ersten neun Monaten 2026 für Firmen aus Deutschland, doppelt so viel wie ein Jahr zuvor, wie aus den am Donnerstag veröffentlichten "League Tables" des Londoner Börsenbetreibers und Finanzdatenanbieters LSEG (LSEG.L) hervorgeht. Auf ihr Konto gehen damit fast 60 Prozent des gesamten Volumens von Fusionen und Übernahmen mit deutscher Beteiligung von 179,3 Milliarden Dollar (Stand: 23. September). Bei fünf der sechs größten Deals kam der Käufer aus dem Ausland. Insgesamt wurden deutsche Unternehmen für 123,1 Milliarden Dollar verkauft, das ist schon jetzt mehr als im gesamten Jahr 2025. Aber auch deutsche Konzerne kauften im Ausland - vor allem in den USA - für 47,1 Milliarden Dollar ein und gaben damit mehr als doppelt so viel aus wie ein Jahr zuvor. Was auffällt: Während der Wert der Fusionen und Übernahmen um 47 Prozent stieg und damit so hoch war wie zuletzt 2018, ist die Zahl der Transaktionen um vier Prozent gesunken. "Wir sehen im laufenden Jahr ein Comeback großer, strategischer Transaktionen", sagte Christopher Droege, Chef des Geschäfts mit Fusionen und Übernahmen bei der US-Investmentbank Goldman Sachs für Deutschland und Österreich der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters. Die Käufer ließen sich dabei von höheren Zinsen, steigenden Anleiherenditen und geopolitischer Unsicherheit nicht beirren. "Größe ist im globalen Wettbewerb zunehmend eine Voraussetzung für Erfolg." Deutsche Unternehmen seien attraktiv: "Insbesondere die Verbindung der hohen industriellen Fertigungskompetenz mit industrieller KI ist eine Chance für die deutsche Wirtschaft", sagte Droege. DIE GRÖSSTEN ÜBERNAHMEN: * Der finnische Aufzughersteller Kone (KNEBV.HE) greift nach dem deutschen Konkurrenten TK Elevator. Kone bietet den beiden Finanzinvestoren Advent und Cinven 20 Milliarden Euro in bar und in eigenen Aktien. Einschließlich Schulden hat die Übernahme einen Wert von 34,4 Milliarden Dollar. Allerdings müssen ihr noch die Kartellbehörden zustimmen - das ist nicht trivial, weil TKE und Kone den Markt zusammen mit zwei Konkurrenten dominieren. Auch die ehemalige Mutter ThyssenKrupp (TKAG.DE) als Minderheitsaktionär würde von einem Verkauf finanziell profitieren. * Der US-Fahrdienst Uber (UBER.N) greift für bis zu 14,6 Milliarden Dollar nach dem Essenslieferdienst Delivery Hero (DHER.DE) . Das Berliner Unternehmen war unter Beschuss von Aktionären gekommen, die den Rückzug von Vorstandschef Niklas Östberg erzwingen wollten. Uber nutzte die Gelegenheit und den von den EU-Kartellbehörden forcierten Anteilsabbau von Großaktionär Prosus (PRX.AS) zum Einstieg und zur Aufstockung seiner Anteile. Der US-Konzern liefert mit "Uber Eats" ebenfalls Essen aus Restaurants nach Hause. Inzwischen läuft ein Übernahmeangebot an alle Delivery-Hero-Aktionäre. Uber hat sich bis Ende der vergangenen Woche bereits 49 Prozent der Anteile gesichert. * Der Pharma- und Technologiekonzern Merck (MRCG.DE) baut sein Life-Science-Geschäft aus und übernimmt den US-Laborausrüster Bio-Techne (TECH.O) für 11,4 Milliarden Dollar. Damit stärkt das Darmstädter Unternehmen seinen Zugang zu wachstumsstarken Märkten wie der Zell- und Gentherapie sowie der Präzisionsdiagnostik. Die Übernahme ist der erste große strategische Schritt des neuen Merck-Chefs Kai Beckmann. * Die Hamburger Containerreederei Hapag-Lloyd (HLAG.DE) will für umgerechnet 8,3 Milliarden Dollar einschließlich Schulden die israelische ZIM Integrated Shipping schlucken. ZIM ist die zehntgrößte Containerreederei weltweit, Hapag-Lloyd die Nummer fünf. Um das Unternehmen aus Haifa hatten auch größere Konkurrenten wie Maersk (MAERSKb.CO) und MSC gebuhlt. * UniCredit (CRDI.MI) hat mit einem Aktientausch-Angebot an die Commerzbank (CBKG.DE) -Aktionäre seinen Anteil an der Frankfurter Bank auf 49 Prozent aufgestockt und sich damit freie Hand für weitere Aktienkäufe am Markt verschafft. UniCredit-Chef Andrea Orcel ringt derzeit um eine Komplettübernahme der zweitgrößten börsennotierten Bank Deutschlands, die er auf lange Sicht mit der Münchner UniCredit-Tochter HypoVereinsbank zusammenführen will. Die bisherige Aufstockung des Anteils wird in den League Tables mit 7,0 Milliarden Dollar bewertet. * Nach dem Heiztechnik-Spezialisten Viessmann wird ein weiteres deutsches Familienunternehmen in die USA verkauft. Der württembergische Ventilatoren- und Lüfter-Hersteller ebm-papst geht für 5,9 Milliarden Dollar an die börsennotierte Madison Air (MAIR.N) aus Chicago, die bereits zu den Kunden des Unternehmens aus Mulfingen gehört. EBM-Papst erhofft sich davon vor allem einen besseren und schnelleren Zugang zum US-Markt, wo das Geschäft mit Rechenzentren besonders boomt. Die Ausrüstung von Rechenzentren steht bereits für rund ein Drittel des Umsatzes von EBM-Papst. * In einem wochenlangen Bieterwettstreit um die Augsburger Volkswagen (VOWG.DE) -Dieselmotorentochter Everllence hat sich der Finanzinvestor Bain Capital durchgesetzt. Der neue Mehrheitseigentümer verspricht sich Rückenwind durch die Energiewende beim Antrieb von Schiffen und durch den steigenden Energiebedarf wegen des Booms bei Rechenzentren. Bain übernimmt 51 Prozent der Anteile. Insidern zufolge wurde Everllence dabei mit deutlich mehr als neun Milliarden Euro bewertet, Volkswagen beziffert den Gesamterlös auf 7,4 Milliarden Euro. Der genaue Transaktionswert lässt sich daraus laut LSEG aber nicht ermitteln, so dass der Deal nicht in der Rangliste auftaucht. DIE ERFOLGREICHSTEN BERATER: * Bei fünf der sechs größten Transaktionen dieses Jahres mischte die US-Investmentbank Goldman Sachs mit - auf Seiten des Käufers oder des Verkäufers. Das macht sie erneut unangefochten zur Nummer eins in der Rangliste der erfolgreichsten Berater. Goldman Sachs beriet in den ersten neun Monaten bei 29 Transaktionen im Wert von 99,0 Milliarden Dollar. Die Deutsche Bank schob sich mit 24 Übernahmen im Wert von 73,7 Milliarden Dollar auf Platz zwei - vor einem Jahr war sie Vierte. Auf den Rängen drei bis fünf folgen erneut drei US-Banken: Bank of America (BofA Securities) mit 18 Mandaten im Volumen von 68,2 Milliarden Dollar, Morgan Stanley (64,8 Milliarden) und JPMorgan (59,0 Milliarden). * Das Geschäft mit Eigenkapital-Emissionen und -Platzierungen (ECM) hat weiter angezogen, bleibt aber aufgrund des Ausbleibens größerer Börsengänge auf niedrigem Niveau. JPMorgan führt vor Goldman Sachs und der Deutschen Bank. * Bei Fremdkapital-Transaktionen verteidigt die Deutsche Bank mit 116 Emissionen im Volumen von 32,4 Milliarden Dollar ihren unangefochtenen Spitzenplatz. Direkt dahinter liegt wieder JPMorgan (21,2 Milliarden Dollar), gefolgt von Barclays (18,2 Milliarden) und BNP Paribas (17,6 Milliarden).

item.title: Isabel Schnabel verso dimissioni Bce - fonti
item.description: Isabel Schnabel, membro del Comitato esecutivo della Banca centrale europea (Bce), lascerà anticipatamente l’istituzione per assumere un incarico di rilievo presso il Fondo monetario internazionale (Fmi).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Isabel Schnabel, membro del Comitato esecutivo della Banca centrale europea (Bce), lascerà anticipatamente l’istituzione per assumere un incarico di rilievo presso il Fondo monetario internazionale (Fmi). L’annuncio è imminente e potrebbe arrivare in giornata, secondo quanto riferito a Reuters da due fonti informate sulla questione. Il mandato di otto anni di Schnabel, responsabile delle operazioni di mercato della Bce, sarebbe dovuto scadere alla fine del 2027, ma il Fmi sarebbe intenzionato a trovare un nuovo direttore del proprio dipartimento di mercato entro la fine di quest’anno, hanno detto le fonti. Bce e Fmi non hanno commentato.

item.title: Ausnahmezustand in russischer Region Krasnodar wegen Drohnenangriffen
item.description: Wegen ukrainischer Drohnenangriffe auf die Infrastruktur für den Getreideexport hat der Gouverneur der südrussischen Agrarregion Krasnodar den Ausnahmezustand ausgerufen. Die massiven Attacken auf die Anlagen hätten den Hafenbetrieb lahmgelegt und die Schifffahrt im Schwarzen Meer gestört, teilte Gouverneur Weniamin Kondratjew laut der Nachrichtenagentur Interfax am Donnerstag mit. Durch den Ausnahmezustand können betroffene Betriebe finanzielle Entschädigungen erhalten.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Wegen ukrainischer Drohnenangriffe auf die Infrastruktur für den Getreideexport hat der Gouverneur der südrussischen Agrarregion Krasnodar den Ausnahmezustand ausgerufen. Die massiven Attacken auf die Anlagen hätten den Hafenbetrieb lahmgelegt und die Schifffahrt im Schwarzen Meer gestört, teilte Gouverneur Weniamin Kondratjew laut der Nachrichtenagentur Interfax am Donnerstag mit. Durch den Ausnahmezustand können betroffene Betriebe finanzielle Entschädigungen erhalten. Den Angaben zufolge können die Landwirte einen Großteil ihrer Ernte nicht verkaufen, was zu einem Überangebot auf dem russischen Getreidemarkt führt. Krasnodar hat in diesem Jahr 11,4 Millionen Tonnen Getreide und Hülsenfrüchte geerntet, fast zwei Millionen Tonnen mehr als im Jahr 2025. Besonders die Hafenstadt Noworossijsk, ein wichtiger Umschlagplatz für russisches Öl und Getreide, ist immer wieder Ziel ukrainischer Drohnenangriffe. Sowohl Russland als auch die Ukraine haben in den vergangenen Monaten ihre Angriffe auf Getreideschiffe im Schwarzen Meer verstärkt, was die Weltmarktpreise in die Höhe trieb. Der Kreml erklärte in dieser Woche, es gebe weitere diplomatische Gespräche über einen Vorschlag der Türkei zur sicheren Durchfahrt von Getreideschiffen im Schwarzen Meer. Bis zu einer Einigung suche Russland nach alternativen Routen für seine Exporte. Im Juli 2022 hatten die Türkei und die UN das sogenannte Schwarzmeer-Getreideabkommen vermittelt, um trotz des Krieges sichere ukrainische Exporte zu ermöglichen. Russland war jedoch im folgenden Jahr aus der Vereinbarung ausgestiegen. Zur Begründung hieß es, dass die eigenen Nahrungsmittel- und Düngemittelexporte behindert würden.

item.title: Letzter Siemens-Vertreter verlässt Aufsichtsrat von Siemens Energy
item.description: Sechs Jahre nach der Abspaltung der Energietechnik-Sparte verlässt der letzte Siemens-Vertreter den Aufsichtsrat der Siemens Energy AG. Der langjährige Siemens-Infrastrukturtechnik-Vorstand Matthias Rebellius scheide zum Monatsende auf eigenen Wunsch aus dem Gremium aus, teilte Siemens Energy am Donnerstag mit. Rebellius' Vorstandsvertrag bei Siemens läuft ebenfalls im September aus. Nachdem der Anteil des Münchner Technologiekonzerns an Siemens Energy auf weniger als fünf Prozent gesunken ist, hat Siemens keinen Anspruch mehr auf einen Sitz im Aufsichtsrat. Der ehemalige Siemens-Chef Joe Kaeser fungiert aber weiter als Aufsichtsratschef.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Sechs Jahre nach der Abspaltung der Energietechnik-Sparte verlässt der letzte Siemens (SIEGn.DE) -Vertreter den Aufsichtsrat der Siemens Energy AG (ENR1n.DE) . Der langjährige Siemens-Infrastrukturtechnik-Vorstand Matthias Rebellius scheide zum Monatsende auf eigenen Wunsch aus dem Gremium aus, teilte Siemens Energy am Donnerstag mit. Rebellius' Vorstandsvertrag bei Siemens läuft ebenfalls im September aus. Nachdem der Anteil des Münchner Technologiekonzerns an Siemens Energy auf weniger als fünf Prozent gesunken ist, hat Siemens keinen Anspruch mehr auf einen Sitz im Aufsichtsrat. Der ehemalige Siemens-Chef Joe Kaeser fungiert aber weiter als Aufsichtsratschef. Nachfolger von Rebellius bei Siemens Energy wird zum 1. Oktober der ehemalige Nokia (NOKIA.HE) -Chef Pekka Lundmark. Das Amtsgericht München habe ihn auf Antrag des Vorstands bestellt, erklärte das Unternehmen.

item.title: Fincantieri-Leonardo, contratto da 3,7 miliardi per due nuovi cacciatorpedinieri della Marina
item.description: Orizzonte Sistemi Navali (Osn), joint venture tra Fincantieri e Leonardo , ha firmato con Occar un contratto del valore complessivo di circa 3,7 miliardi di euro per lo sviluppo e la costruzione di due cacciatorpedinieri di nuova generazione destinati alla Marina Militare italiana.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Orizzonte Sistemi Navali (Osn), joint venture tra Fincantieri (FCT.MI) e Leonardo (LDOF.MI) , ha firmato con Occar un contratto del valore complessivo di circa 3,7 miliardi di euro per lo sviluppo e la costruzione di due cacciatorpedinieri di nuova generazione destinati alla Marina Militare italiana. Il contratto, si legge in una nota congiunta, comprende circa 1,3 miliardi di euro di opzioni e sarà seguito nelle prossime settimane da contratti di subfornitura per circa 1,8 miliardi a Fincantieri e circa 1,7 miliardi a Leonardo, anch'essi comprensivi di quote opzionali. "Le nuove navi saranno progettate per operare all’interno di forze multinazionali altamente interconnesse e saranno caratterizzate da elevati livelli di digitalizzazione, automazione e integrazione tra sensori, sistemi d’arma, sistemi di comando e controllo multidominio e sistemi di gestione della piattaforma", spiega la nota. Le nuove unità DDX sostituiranno progressivamente i cacciatorpedinieri della classe Horizon e saranno progettate per operare in scenari ad alta intensità, con capacità avanzate di difesa aerea e antimissile, integrazione multidominio e impiego di sistemi unmanned. Fincantieri agirà come system integrator della piattaforma navale, mentre Leonardo fornirà il sistema di combattimento. La consegna delle due unità è prevista rispettivamente nel 2033 e nel 2035. [USN:BIA2NtTCT TEXT:"Comunicato integrale"]

item.title: VW-Tochter MOIA startet Robotaxi-Fahrten in den USA
item.description: Die Volkswagen-Tochter MOIA America hat in den USA ihren ersten Passagierbetrieb mit selbstfahrenden Taxis gestartet. Zusammen mit dem Mobilitätsanbieter Beep bietet das Unternehmen Fahrten in der Gemeinde Lake Nona in Orlando im US-Bundesstaat Florida an, wie die Firmen am Donnerstag mitteilten. Die autonom fahrenden Fahrzeuge vom Typ ID.Buzz sind mit einem System des Entwicklers Mobileye ausgestattet. In der aktuellen Phase befindet sich zur Sicherheit noch ein Mensch an Bord. Fahrgäste können die Fahrten über eine App von Beep auf drei festgelegten Routen buchen.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Die Volkswagen-Tochter MOIA America hat in den USA ihren ersten Passagierbetrieb mit selbstfahrenden Taxis gestartet. Zusammen mit dem Mobilitätsanbieter Beep bietet das Unternehmen Fahrten in der Gemeinde Lake Nona in Orlando im US-Bundesstaat Florida an, wie die Firmen am Donnerstag mitteilten. Die autonom fahrenden Fahrzeuge vom Typ ID.Buzz sind mit einem System des Entwicklers Mobileye (MBLY.O) ausgestattet. In der aktuellen Phase befindet sich zur Sicherheit noch ein Mensch an Bord. Fahrgäste können die Fahrten über eine App von Beep auf drei festgelegten Routen buchen. Florida gilt als einer der US-Bundesstaaten mit den liberalsten Gesetzen für das Testen autonomer Fahrzeuge. MOIA America bereitet zudem in Los Angeles und Austin den Start kommerzieller Dienste vor und nimmt dort Testfahrten vor. Damit tritt die VW-Tochter gegen schon länger auf dem Robotaxi-Markt etablierte Konkurrenten wie die Alphabet (GOOGL.O) -Tochter Waymo und Tesla (TSLA.O) an, die nach Testphasen den kommerziellen Betrieb vorantreiben.

item.title: Schnabel vai deixar o cargo no BC dando início a uma reorganização do conselho, dizendo fontes
item.description: Isabel Schnabel, membro do Banco Central Europeu, vai anunciar sua renúncia nesta quinta-feira para ingressar no Fundo Monetário Internacional, informaram duas fontes à Reuters, dando início a uma longa reorganização dos cargos mais importantes do conselho do banco.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Isabel Schnabel, membro do Banco Central Europeu, vai anunciar sua renúncia nesta quinta-feira para ingressar no Fundo Monetário Internacional, informaram duas fontes à Reuters, dando início a uma longa reorganização dos cargos mais importantes do conselho do banco. Schnabel, chefe das operações de mercado do BCE, deveria permanecer no cargo até o final de 2027, mas o FMI estava empenhado em encontrar um novo diretor para seu departamento de mercado até o final deste ano, disseram as fontes. Tanto o BCE quanto o FMI se recusaram a comentar. A saída de Schnabel, da Alemanha, dá início ao que deve ser um complicado jogo de xadrez político, já que o economista-chefe do BCE, Philip Lane, deve deixar o cargo em maio, enquanto a presidente do BCE, Christine Lagarde — ela própria alvo de rumores persistentes de renúncia —, deixará o cargo até outubro próximo, no máximo. Isso sugere que a substituição de Schnabel fará parte de um acordo político mais amplo, e não de uma simples nomeação, já que Alemanha, Espanha, Holanda e França estão disputando assentos de poder no conselho. Embora tecnicamente qualquer país possa disputar o cargo de Schnabel, os três principais do bloco — Alemanha, França e Itália — têm, de fato, um assento permanente no conselho. No entanto, se a Alemanha simplesmente substituísse Schnabel por outro candidato, isso significa que Berlim não disputaria a presidência do BCE assim que o cargo de Lagarde ficar vago. É por isso que fontes próximas ao assunto afirmam que qualquer acordo sobre o cargo de Schnabel provavelmente envolverá também as outras duas posições. A Espanha está fazendo lobby para que o gerente geral do Banco de Compensações Internacionais, Pablo Hernández de Cos, torne-se o próximo presidente do BCE, enquanto a Holanda defende Klaas Knot, ex-presidente do banco central do país. A Alemanha estava considerando o presidente do Bundesbank, Joachim Nagel, para a presidência, mas seu compromisso parece ter enfraquecido recentemente e o país pode optar por um cargo diferente. Enquanto isso, a França, que já proporcionou ao BCE dois presidentes — Lagarde e Jean-Claude Trichet —, espera conseguir o cargo de economista-chefe, informaram fontes anteriormente. (Reportagem de Balazs Koranyi e Francesco Canepa)

item.title: Braves' Tyler Mahle eager to keep up stellar form vs. Reds
item.description: Tyler Mahle, Atlanta's most impactful trade deadline acquisition this season, will take the mound on Thursday when the Braves host the Cincinnati Reds in their final home game of the season.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Tyler Mahle, Atlanta's most impactful trade deadline acquisition this season, will take the mound on Thursday when the Braves host the Cincinnati Reds in their final home game of the season. The Braves (93-65) won Wednesday's game 3-2 in 10 innings to square the three-game series at one victory apiece. Cincinnati (73-85) has lost three of its last four games and is 29-33 since the All-Star break. Mahle (7-10, 3.81 ERA) will be opposed by Cincinnati's Brady Singer (6-15, 5.67) on Thursday in a battle of right-handers. Mahle, obtained from San Francisco at the deadline, has pitched his way into position as the No. 2 man in the Atlanta rotation behind Chris Sale. He was 3-9 with a 5.13 ERA in 18 starts with San Francisco, but since joining Atlanta is 4-1 with a 1.28 ERA in eight starts. In his last start on Friday at Houston, Mahle pitched six innings and allowed only one run on three hits. He has not given up more than two runs in any start since joining the Braves and has been caught each time by veteran Sean Murphy. "He can throw strikes with all of his pitches," Atlanta manager Walt Weiss said. "Murph has done a nice job with him, he enjoys catching him. He can throw the ball where he wants to. It's nice for a catcher when guys can do that." Mahle's lone career appearance against the Reds came this season. He allowed a season-high eight runs in four innings to take the loss on April 15. Singer will look to end a two-game losing streak during which he has allowed 15 runs in 7 1/3 innings. He gave up seven runs in 3 1/3 innings - his second-shortest stint of the season - in his last outing on Thursday against the Los Angeles Dodgers. "I think the biggest thing, try to figure out a way to have some command and put the ball where you want to and just keep working," Singer said. "We're doing stuff during the week, trying to figure stuff out. Matt Tracy (assistant pitching coach) is trying to help me out as much as he can and we work on those things and we've had good weeks. It's just not really carrying over to the games." Singer faced the Braves on May 30 and worked five innings, allowing three runs on four hits and four walks. In five career starts against Atlanta, Singer is 1-4 with a 5.46 ERA. The Braves activated setup man Robert Suarez from the injured list on Wednesday and optioned fellow right-hander Owen Murphy to Triple-A Gwinnett. Suarez missed 80 games with right elbow inflammation. He pitched one inning and allowed a run in his return. Atlanta right fielder Ronald Acuna Jr. is expected to be back in the lineup on Thursday. He missed Wednesday's game after fouling a ball off his left shin on Tuesday. Acuna wanted to play on Wednesday, but Weiss opted to give him an additional day off as a precautionary measure. Atlanta's Mauricio Dubon had two hits on Wednesday and extended his hitting streak to 11 games. Cincinnati's Elly De La Cruz did not reach base on Wednesday and needs one homer and one steal to become the fourth 30-30 player in franchise history. --Field Level Media

item.title: Tech and world leaders split over AI
item.description: Hello!
item.dc:creator: Sharon Kimathi
item.content:encoded: Hello! It has been quite a dramatic United Nations General Assembly this week as world leaders gathered in New York for their annual diplomatic talks. But some were not so diplomatic. I’m sure by now most of you have seen clips of US President Donald Trump’s speech where he said he could annihilate Iran without a peace deal and predicted one would be reached after US midterm elections on November 3 when the makeup of Congress will be decided.[USN:L1N45E0M0 TEXT:" Click here"] for a summary of what else Trump said at the UN. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian accused Trump of a "bullying mentality", saying Iran would not surrender in the war with the US but remained open to diplomacy to end the conflict. Click here to sign up to the Reuters Iran Briefing newsletter to stay informed with the latest developments and analysis of the Iran war. But today’s focus is not about the war of words. Instead, we look at the discussions around artificial intelligence that took place between tech companies and world leaders. What did the tech heads say? The world's leading [USN:L6N45E0VV TEXT:"AI companies warned"] the United Nations Security Council on Wednesday of the risks posed by AI to humanity, appealing for governments to work together to manage the increasingly powerful technology. [USN:L4N456128 TEXT:"AI industry leaders are split"] over how fast companies should develop the increasingly powerful technology, as Anthropic's Dario Amodei, OpenAI's Sam Altman and xAI's Elon Musk call for a coordinated slowdown. Meta's Mark Zuckerberg appeared to break away from other AI leaders, favouring market-led safeguards, while Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang dismissed the need for new regulations. Amodei told the 15-member council, which is charged with maintaining international peace and security, that if managed poorly, he believed "AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole." "For all the differences of the people in this room, we must put aside those differences in order to confront this global opportunity and global threat that is being presented to us at the same time. No leader, no company and no nation can manage this alone," Amodei said. Hugging Face co-founder Clément Delangue highlighted the role of AI tools in defending against cyberattacks, citing an incident in which US OpenAI's AI agents breached Hugging Face's infrastructure after escaping their testing environment. "We were attacked by AI, but more importantly, we defended ourselves with AI," he told the council. Delangue said Hugging Face relied on a Chinese AI model to help defend against the attack by OpenAI's AI agents because it faced fewer restrictions than comparable US tools. His remarks underscored the growing presence of Chinese AI products, which have gained users globally in part because they can offer lower-cost alternatives to American models. What about heads of state and government? Governments around the world have struggled to keep pace with rapid advances in AI. The US and China, the two leading powers in AI development, have taken different approaches to oversight. Trump has argued that the US does not need new AI-specific regulations, while China has imposed rules governing AI algorithms and training data, including requirements that AI-generated content be clearly labeled. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese told reporters in New York that an AI agent developed by OpenAI[USN:L4N45F1E8 TEXT:" infiltrated"] an Australian government website in June, accessing public and non-public files. British [USN:L8N45E18S TEXT:"Prime Minister Andy Burnham"] told the United Nations that Britain was ready to lead an international effort to establish AI standards, citing concerns that the technology could outpace safeguards and pose mounting national security risks. "We've all[USN:L4N456128 TEXT:" heard the warnings"] – which we must heed," he said in his inaugural speech to the UN General Assembly. "I know how worried people are. So we have to rise to this moment." Talking Points Indonesia’s Borneo wildfires: Click here for an insightful photo essay on the all-women firefighting group called The Power of Mama who are at the front lines of battling the worst wildfires in 11 years on the Indonesian islands of Borneo and Sumatra. The fires have been raging longer than usual this year and have been made worse by the drought-inducing El Niño weather pattern. Palestinian olives bulldozed: Palestinian villagers wailed over the mangled remains of their olive trees after Israel's military uprooted them with bulldozers, days ahead of the annual olive harvest in the occupied West Bank. Olives are the backbone of Palestinian agriculture, a sector that accounts for around 8% of GDP and more than 60,000 jobs, according to the Palestinian Authority's agriculture ministry. [USN:L8N45F1FN TEXT:"Click here"] to read the full Reuters story. Mexico Hurricane Polo: Residents of Mexico's Pacific beach towns were preparing for heavy rain and winds of 145 mph (230 kph) as [USN:L8N45F0LO TEXT:"Hurricane Polo, a powerful Category 4 storm"], tracked northwestward just offshore, threatening flooding and mudslides along the country's southwestern coast. Michigan climate lawsuit: US District Judge Jane Beckering in Grand Rapids rejected a [USN:L1N45F002 TEXT:"lawsuit against BP, Chevron, Exxon and Shell"], filed in January by Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel, which accused the major oil companies of colluding to forestall competition in renewable energy, including electric vehicles, a decision in line with prior rulings in similar cases. US critical minerals funding: The US Export-Import Bank plans to fund up to [USN:L1N45E106 TEXT:"$7 billion worth of critical minerals"] and energy projects in Argentina as it seeks more access to Western hemisphere energy and critical minerals, according to a document seen by Reuters. The move is part of a push to deepen economic cooperation between Washington and Buenos Aires. In Conversation Woochong Um, CEO of the multi-sector Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet, shares his thoughts on this year’s UN General Assembly: "The world faces profound challenges, from climate change to inequality, and the rapid transformations brought by artificial intelligence. “The truth is that these challenges are profoundly interconnected. “While the world grapples with the future prospect of AI super intelligence, we must also acknowledge the extraordinary opportunity AI offers to build a more prosperous, inclusive and equitable world, today. “That starts with access to electricity. Currently, more than 650 million people live without any access to electricity at all. By making power grids smarter, AI can reduce outages, increase efficiencies, show us where to integrate renewables and in doing so, bring reliable electricity to communities that have waited for it for far too long. “We absolutely need guardrails around AI to ensure our safer future. And we absolutely need it to accelerate our efforts today to power clean, abundant, economic growth in emerging and developing economies.” ESG Spotlight Environmental groups and volunteers saving mussels from shallow waters in the Czech Republic take today’s spotlight. Operators of [USN:L8N45F0XS TEXT:"the Slapy dam"], upstream from Prague, were forced to reduce its water level to record lows due to a severe drought that hit the nation this year, to maintain flows downstream. Volunteers rushed to rescue the protected mussels from the newly exposed banks into deeper waters elsewhere. Mussels act as important filters for the water, keeping rivers and streams clean. Think your friend or colleague should know about us? Forward this newsletter to them. They can also subscribe here.

item.title: US to provide critical but more limited capabilities to NATO, top commander says
item.description: NATO's top commander said on Thursday the United States would continue to provide "critical but more limited capabilities" to the alliance as Europeans take up a greater role in defending the continent.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: NATO's top commander said on Thursday the United States would continue to provide "critical but more limited capabilities" to the alliance as Europeans take up a greater role in defending the continent. U.S. Air Force General Alexus Grynkewich, NATO's Supreme Allied Commander Europe, was speaking in a phone interview with Reuters en route to a change of command ceremony at a NATO headquarters in Norfolk, Virginia, where a British army general will take over from a U.S. Navy vice admiral.

item.title: UN rights chief says civilians are bearing the brunt of fighting in Yemen
item.description: Civilians are being hardest hit by surging violence in Yemen between Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces and Iran-backed Houthis, the UN human rights chief said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Civilians are being hardest hit by [USN:L1N45G08F TEXT:"surging violence"] in Yemen between Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces and Iran-backed Houthis, the UN human rights chief said on Thursday. The latest fighting marks a sharp escalation in Yemen's civil war, which had largely been frozen since a 2022 truce. Violence has flared along old front lines in recent weeks, including around Taiz as the Houthis swept south along the Red Sea coast, prompting a [USN:L6N45E0CP TEXT:"humanitarian crisis "]with over 130,000 people displaced and some [USN:L6N45A0K6 TEXT:"fleeing to Africa across the Red Sea"]. UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk said his office has documented the killing of 32 civilians, including 15 children and 3 women, since August in fighting, including drone and missile strikes. "Civilians are now bearing the brunt of this latest upsurge in fighting," Turk said in a statement, without giving a breakdown of who was responsible for the casualties. A total of 125 people were documented by his office as killed or wounded in the latest flareup in the conflict. Both sides allege that hundreds have been killed in fighting over the past weeks, without providing details. The statement said the UN human rights office had documented three attacks by Ansar Allah, the formal name for the Houthi movement, on sites for internally displaced people since August. It was not immediately clear if the UN toll included any deaths or injuries from those incidents. Houthi spokesperson Mohammed Abdulsalam said the UN human rights office was no longer impartial, accusing it of ignoring what he described as Saudi bombardment in Yemen that had targeted public facilities. He cited what he said was the targeting of inmates at a correctional facility in al-Hazm in al-Jawf province, as well as homes and schools in several areas. He said the UN allegations were false and unsupported by evidence. More than 70 UN staff are being detained by Houthis in Yemen, some of whom have been held for many years. Turk called for their release and urged all the warring parties to protect civilians. Saudi officials have repeatedly said the country's forces do not target civilians in Yemen. Saudi Arabia's diplomatic mission to the UN in Geneva did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

item.title: Dinamarca prevê que Rússia intensifique guerra híbrida nos próximos meses, aponta serviço de inteligência
item.description: A Rússia deve intensificar sua guerra híbrida contra o Ocidente nos próximos meses, afirmou o serviço de inteligência de defesa da Dinamarca em uma nova avaliação de ameaças divulgada nesta quinta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Soren Jeppesen
item.content:encoded: A Rússia deve intensificar sua guerra híbrida contra o Ocidente nos próximos meses, afirmou o serviço de inteligência de defesa da Dinamarca em uma nova avaliação de ameaças divulgada nesta quinta-feira. A guerra híbrida e a sabotagem em solo europeu voltaram a ganhar destaque depois que a Alemanha recentemente culpou a Rússia por uma tentativa de ataque com drones no Aeroporto de Leipzig/Halle, levando os membros da União Europeia a pedir novas sanções contra a Rússia. Moscou negou repetidamente qualquer envolvimento em guerra híbrida, operações de sabotagem em países da Otan ou planejamento de qualquer confronto. A embaixada da Rússia na Dinamarca não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário. O serviço de inteligência de defesa afirmou que a Rússia realizará ataques mais frequentes contra o Ocidente e a Otan, “com consequências mais graves para os países visados do que no passado”. Acrescentou que há “um risco baixo, mas crescente”, de que a Rússia lance um ataque militar limitado contra um ou vários países da Otan que fazem fronteira com a Rússia. “Um ataque militar limitado seria uma medida desesperada por parte da Rússia e, assim como os ataques híbridos intensificados, poderia ocorrer nos próximos meses”, afirmou. Tais ataques poderiam incluir ataques isolados com armas de longo alcance, como drones ou mísseis, contra infraestruturas que dão apoio à Ucrânia, ou operações de bandeira falsa utilizando drones de fabricação ucraniana, disse o chefe do serviço de inteligência, Thomas Ahrenkiel, em uma coletiva de imprensa. Ele disse que a Rússia também poderia enviar um número limitado de tropas para uma área de fronteira da Otan, possivelmente sob o pretexto de proteger minorias russas. “O objetivo não é tomar o país, mas dividir a Otan”, declarou ele.

item.title: US current account deficit widens sharply in second quarter
item.description: The US current account deficit widened sharply in the second quarter amid a surge in imports of goods, government data showed on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US current account deficit widened sharply in the second quarter amid a surge in imports of goods, government data showed on Thursday. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis said the current account deficit, which measures the flow of goods, services and investments into and out of the country, increased $33.4 billion, or 15.7%, to $246.0 billion last quarter. Data for the January-March quarter was revised lower to show the shortfall at $212.6 billion instead of the previously estimated $226.8 billion. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the current account gap would widen to $255.0 billion. The second-quarter current account deficit represented 3.0% of gross domestic product, up from 2.7% in the January-March quarter. It peaked at 6.3% in the third quarter of 2006. While the current account deficit has no impact on the dollar, given the greenback's status as a reserve currency, concerns are growing over the nation's ballooning twin deficits. Goods imports shot up by $67.4 billion to $931.6 billion. That outpaced a $27.1 billion increase in exports of goods to $640.3 billion. As a result, the goods trade deficit widened $40.4 billion to $291.3 billion. Trade subtracted 1.14 percentage points from gross domestic product in the second quarter and has been a drag for three straight quarters. The primary income balance narrowed to $11.4 billion last quarter from $15.8 billion in the January-March quarter. Primary income receipts rose to $416.2 billion from $391.5 billion in the prior quarter. Primary income payments increased to $427.6 billion from $407.3 billion in the first quarter. The nation's international investment position, the difference between US residents' foreign financial assets and liabilities, deteriorated slightly to a $22.42 trillion deficit at the end of the second quarter from a $21.27 trillion shortfall in the first quarter. Assets totaled $46.97 trillion, while liabilities amounted to $69.39 trillion.

item.title: US to seek Supreme Court relief after court blocked third-country removals, Blanche says
item.description: The Trump administration will appeal to the US Supreme Court a lower court ruling rejecting a policy that allowed authorities to rapidly deport migrants to countries other than their own, US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration will appeal to the US Supreme Court a lower court ruling rejecting a policy that allowed authorities to rapidly deport migrants to countries other than their own, US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday. "Without even allowing the government a chance to respond, and in the dark of night, a federal appeals court blocked us from conducting all third-country removals of illegal aliens, an entirely legal and invaluable tool to stem the tide of illegal immigration," he wrote on in an X post. "We will immediately seek relief from the Supreme Court, which previously granted a stay in this very same case." Under President Donald Trump, the administration has entered into a series of agreements that have allowed it to send more than 25,000 migrants to at least 29 third countries, in many cases Mexico, according to Third Country Deportation Watch, a project run by Refugees International and Human Rights First. A US federal appeals court rejected policy on Friday. A three-judge panel of the 1st US Circuit Court of Appeals in Boston largely upheld a February decision by a lower court that declared the Department of Homeland Security's policy unlawful. The ruling came in a class action lawsuit filed by migrants subject to deportation orders that has become a key test of what due-process protections the government must provide before removing people to countries with which they have no connection.

item.title: Guardians, against Red Sox, make another try at clinching AL playoff spot
item.description: A nor'easter is expected to hit Boston over the weekend, but the Red Sox and Cleveland Guardians have played with an October-like chill in the air this week.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: A nor'easter is expected to hit Boston over the weekend, but the Red Sox and Cleveland Guardians have played with an October-like chill in the air this week. With their eyes on the start of the postseason, the two American League contenders will complete their competitive three-game, penultimate series of the regular season on Thursday night at Fenway Park. The Red Sox (85-73) snapped a three-game slide with a 1-0 win on Wednesday. Andruw Monasterio hit the go-ahead RBI single in the sixth inning after Sonny Gray pitched six shutout frames, lifting Boston to its AL-leading 17th shutout. "You (have to) keep guys out there, engaged and ready to go," Red Sox manager Chad Tracy said. "I told the guys before, we earned the right to be in position to be able to line things up. That being said, we still want to go out and win the games." The series will conclude with the rubber game, as Cleveland (82-76) was a 3-2 winner in the opener on Tuesday. Given his postgame comments, the Red Sox hope to have avoided a scare regarding center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela, who left his first game back from the injured list with right hamstring tightness. A quad injury sent him to the IL on Sept. 3. "Not even close," Rafaela said of the severity comparison of the two injuries. "I think it was just a cramp." After the game, Tracy said Rafaela would have an MRI exam on Thursday. Left-hander Ranger Suarez (8-4, 3.27 ERA), who will start for Boston on Thursday, carries a three-game win streak after a 5 2/3-inning outing Friday against the AL East champion Tampa Bay Rays. Suarez struck out five and allowed one run, working around three hits and five walks in a 4-2 victory. "He's a very good competitor, a good pitcher that even when he gets traffic, you trust that he's going to find his way through it," Tracy said of Suarez, who has surrendered just two runs across his last 19 2/3 innings. His ERA in three September starts is 0.92. Suarez is 1-1 with a 4.00 ERA in four career appearances (three starts) against Cleveland, including a May 31 road outing in which he struck out 10 and allowed four runs across five frames in a 9-4 win. The Guardians are on the verge of sealing their postseason berth after entering Wednesday with a magic number of two, needing a win themselves and a loss by either the Texas Rangers or Houston Astros to clinch. Both Texas and Houston lost, leaving the Guardians with a magic number of one to make the playoffs. That's the same as the Chicago White Sox. If both win on Thursday, they both will earn a postseason berth. Cleveland, which had a six-game winning streak snapped on Wednesday, has a one-game lead over Chicago in the race for the AL Central title, and the White Sox own the division tiebreaker. "We know we control our own destiny still," Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said. "So, I like where we are. We've got four games left, and we have a chance to get in. That's all you can ask for." Vogt's lineup managed five singles on Wednesday, including two by leadoff hitter Steven Kwan, who has hits in 13 of his past 15 games, with a .373 average over that span. The Guardians entered the series without a scheduled starter for Thursday, but Vogt determined that Daniel Espino (0-0, 4.73 ERA) will open before Joey Cantillo (10-9, 3.74) pitches in a bulk role. That combination was used in a 5-3 win over the Athletics last Friday, with Espino allowing three runs in the first inning and Cantillo firing six shutout, two-hit frames. "The biggest difference is that you don't have as much time to get ready," Cantillo said of the difference between being a starter and reliever. Cantillo is 1-0 with a 3.38 ERA in eight career innings against the Red Sox, and Espino has not faced them. --Field Level Media

item.title: Infantino looks set to stay, but FIFA faces a new war over power
item.description: The battle to force Gianni Infantino out of FIFA may be nearly all over just a few weeks after his opponents thought they would dethrone the president of world soccer's governing body, but the war over how much power he can exercise may only be beginning.
item.dc:creator: Julien Pretot
item.content:encoded: The battle to force Gianni Infantino out of FIFA may be nearly all over just a few weeks after his opponents thought they would [USN:L6N44H116 TEXT:"dethrone"] the president of world soccer's governing body, but the war over how much power he can exercise may only be beginning. Senior figures in world football increasingly see the crisis triggered by Infantino's abandoned private-investment plan shifting away from the question of succession and towards a struggle over the terms of his continued presidency. One outcome could be a governance compromise under which Infantino remains in office but gives up some power. The other possibility is a prolonged “hot-cold war” in which clubs, confederations, player representatives and national associations challenge FIFA repeatedly over competitions, money and control of the international calendar. “What is clear now ... is that he’s going nowhere,” a senior world football executive told Reuters. “A hot-cold war is a very real problem for FIFA and for world football.” A veteran international sports executive, who has spent decades working with governing bodies, offered a similar assessment, saying Infantino was “hanging on” but questioning how FIFA could operate if many of the game’s most powerful countries and institutions remained opposed to him. “You would have effectively a civil war within the governance which I cannot recall in a sports body before,” the executive said. “Unprecedented.” That possible scenario of a prolonged and potentially damaging cold war within world football was independently corroborated to Reuters by two other senior football officials. The prospect points to a potentially paradoxical outcome to a crisis that at its height threatened Infantino’s position: he could survive politically while presiding over a governing body in which some of football’s biggest stakeholders seek to constrain what he can actually do. “Does he become a lame duck?” the veteran executive asked. TRUST STILL BROKEN There is little indication that Infantino’s attempt this week to draw a line under the crisis has repaired the rupture. In a letter to the FIFA Council and the presidents of all 211 member associations, Infantino proposed that the Council consider commissioning an [USN:L1N45D0SB TEXT:"independent external review"] of FIFA’s governance framework for major strategic initiatives. He also proposed consultations with confederations, associations and other stakeholders over strengthening decision-making and said he remained fully committed to leading FIFA. Several European federations quickly [USN:L6N45E0RY TEXT:"dismissed"] the move, and UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin issued a [USN:L6N45F0FH TEXT:"stern assessment"] on Wednesday. “The project that shattered the unity of world football may be abolished, but the trust it broke has not returned,” Ceferin said in a video address to the Portugal Football Summit. “Trust in our sport rests on three pillars: unity, transparency, and governance that serves the many, not the few.” “Football is not for sale,” he added. Ceferin did not name Infantino but his remarks were a clear reference to the proposal to sell a 20% stake in FIFA’s commercial rights, including rights linked to the World Cup, to private investors. The project was dropped in July after opposition from European soccer's governing body UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and North American confederation CONCACAF. ATTRITION For 56-year-old Swiss-Italian Infantino, that leaves one route to a less confrontational settlement, which is a reform substantial enough to persuade his opponents that power inside FIFA has genuinely shifted. The senior world football executive said one possible outcome could be the creation of a new body or structure that diluted the authority of the president. Infantino’s governance proposals were the “bare minimum” needed to give him room to remain in office, the executive said, adding that the question was whether he would accept meaningful changes. How far any compromise could go would depend on “how much Infantino is willing to cede” and how much his opponents were willing to fight to take away, the world football executive said. There is historical irony in such an outcome. Reforms introduced after the downfall of former FIFA chief Sepp Blatter were intended in part to reduce the power concentrated in the presidency. Yet senior figures now see another battle developing over how much authority the FIFA president should wield. If no settlement is reached, the alternative could be attritional rather than spectacular. The world football executive said clubs could fight FIFA over the Club World Cup, financial distributions and player release; player representatives could challenge the calendar; national associations could obstruct initiatives; and major confederations could contest attempts to expand or reshape FIFA competitions. “Maybe it seems like we’re boiling down to two options now,” the executive said. “One, a compromise where Gianni gives up some of his power and there are some new bodies that are created or, two, a permanent hot-cold war where all the stakeholders just fight every issue.” That could include expanded World Cups, bigger or more frequent Club World Cups and commercial distribution decisions, the executive said. The result would not necessarily be a formal break with FIFA. Instead, opponents could make every major initiative harder to deliver. The veteran sports executive said the challenge went to the heart of how global governing bodies function. “The importance of unity. Keeping these monster sports organisations together, they are not political parties,” the executive said. “This will be new territory.” INFANTINO REBUILDS There is another reason the focus is shifting towards life with Infantino rather than replacing him: his position appears to have strengthened since the crisis first erupted. A national association president, who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity, believes Infantino’s opponents missed their best opportunity when the backlash was at its peak and that he is now rebuilding support ahead of the March election. The FIFA president has a succession of opportunities in the coming months to meet national association leaders at tournaments, congresses and confederation events, including several gatherings in Africa. The association president expects Infantino to use those meetings to maintain support among football leaders through to the FIFA presidential election in March 2027. The political significance of smaller associations has also been highlighted by a proposal from Ceferin and CONCACAF President Victor Montagliani for FIFA to distribute at least $10 million from its [USN:L6N45A0ZG TEXT:"reserves"] to each of its 211 member associations during the next financial cycle. For many associations heavily reliant on FIFA funding, such sums could be transformative. If Infantino is reelected, the association president believes some federations that have opposed him may eventually become less hostile, concluding there is little to gain from four years of permanent confrontation. That possibility means a "cold war" is not inevitable.

item.title: Fed's Hammack warns inflation pressures remain tilted to upside
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack said on Thursday that inflation pressures remain elevated and the longer this situation persists, the harder it will be to bring price pressures back to target.
item.dc:creator: Michael Derby
item.content:encoded: Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack said on Thursday that inflation pressures remain elevated and the longer this situation persists, the harder it will be to bring price pressures back to target. “Current conditions in the United States indicate that output is growing at a solid pace and the labor market remains close to my definition of maximum employment, but inflation remains elevated,” Hammack said in comments opening a conference at her bank. “The inflation outlook continues to be highly uncertain, with risks tilted to the upside” and “the longer that high inflation persists, the more challenging and costly it can be to bring it back down,” she said.

item.title: India eases foreign investor access to commodity derivatives, expands scope of portfolio managers
item.description: India on Thursday allowed foreign investors to trade in physically settled contracts, giving them greater access to non-farm commodity contracts as the country looks to increase liquidity and better align the market with global counterparts.
item.dc:creator: Jayshree Pyasi
item.content:encoded: India on Thursday allowed foreign investors to trade in physically settled contracts, giving them greater access to non-farm commodity contracts as the country looks to increase liquidity and better align the market with global counterparts. Markets regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India also allowed portfolio managers based in the country to manage global assets, complementing the government's drive to attract overseas fund management activity. Under the new rules, portfolio managers can also invest in global and to-be-listed securities, in line with allowances for mutual funds and alternative investment funds. Overseas investors currently cannot participate in contracts linked to crude oil, natural gas, gold or silver if they are settled by actual delivery of the underlying goods, largely due to operational constraints. SEBI said it has approved foreign investors to square-off or roll-over positions at least three days before contract expiry. Any positions left open would be automatically transferred to designated trading members, preventing overseas investors from entering the delivery process. The move is expected to boost bullion trading volumes by facilitating foreign investor participation and aligning India with other major markets. Since foreign investors were allowed into cash-settled commodity derivatives in 2022, liquidity in crude oil and natural gas options has risen significantly. They accounted for a growing share of open interest, regulatory data showed. For India's commodities exchange, MCX, energy contracts remain one of the exchange's key growth engines with energy derivatives turnover rising 29% in fiscal ending March 2026.

item.title: PB Fintech to cut costs, slow hiring after India insurance commission caps
item.description: PB Fintech expects India's proposed caps on insurance commissions to severely affect its non-life insurance business, which may lead to spending cuts and a slowdown in hiring, co-founder and group CEO Yashish Dahiya told analysts on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Ashwin Manikandan
item.content:encoded: PB Fintech (PBFI.NS) expects India's [USN:L4N45G0ER TEXT:"proposed"] caps on insurance commissions to severely affect its non-life insurance business, which may lead to spending cuts and a slowdown in hiring, co-founder and group CEO Yashish Dahiya told analysts on Thursday. Shares of Indian insurance distributors and lenders with sizeable insurance distribution income [USN:L4N45G0A1 TEXT:"fell"] following the news, led by a 36% plunge in PB Fintech, the parent of insurance platform Policybazaar. The stock recorded its biggest one-day fall, wiping out more than 314 billion rupees ($3.27 billion) in market capitalisation. The proposals, set out in a consultation paper released on Wednesday, would reintroduce commission caps across life, health and motor insurance that the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India scrapped in 2023. The reforms aim to lower policy costs and curb mis-selling. However, analysts said these could disrupt established distribution models and weigh on growth in an industry that relies heavily on agents and banks to sell policies. PB Fintech said it would respond by managing costs more closely and focusing on profitability. "In terms of general insurance, it is between one-third to 40% of what we have today. So that's a very serious impact on revenue," Dahiya said, adding that the company would reassess spending. "There may be opportunities for rationalisation in digital marketing, brand spending, sales and customer support." The company may also explore new revenue streams and, over the longer term, consider entering insurance manufacturing, Dahiya said. "It becomes a little harder for me to justify not having a manufacturing entity of my own because this somewhat takes away the trust in the fact that distributors would be rewarded for the quality of business they create." PB Fintech said it would not resort to mass layoffs but could slow hiring. The company hired about 6,000 people in the first half of the year, Dahiya said, adding that it might have hired closer to 2,000 had the rules been known earlier. "We run the company for long-term growth and we will calibrate that growth to the new reality." The company could seek to monetise its hospital and garage networks, along with technology, underwriting and claims-related services, he said. PB Fintech expects no impact in fiscal 2027, but fiscal 2028 could be a potential period of "challenges and discovery," if the new rules come into force by then.

item.title: Ibovespa oscila pouco na abertura com exterior no foco
item.description: O Ibovespa oscilava pouco nos primeiros negócios nesta quinta-feira, com investidores ainda monitorando o movimento dos títulos do Tesouro dos Estados Unidos e na expectativa de encontro entre os presidentes norte-americano, Donald Trump, e chinês, Xi Jinping.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Ibovespa oscilava pouco nos primeiros negócios nesta quinta-feira, com investidores ainda monitorando o movimento dos títulos do Tesouro dos Estados Unidos e na expectativa de encontro entre os presidentes norte-americano, Donald Trump, e chinês, Xi Jinping. No Brasil, a pauta incluía o Relatório de Política Monetária do Banco Central, que mostrou redução na projeção de crescimento econômico em 2026 para 1,8%, de 2,0% estimados em junho. Para 2027, o BC estima expansão de 1,4%. Às 10h05, o Ibovespa (.BVSP) , referência do mercado acionário brasileiro, registrava acréscimo de 0,12%, a 186.028,10 pontos, com Petrobras (PETR3.SA) novamente entre as principais contribuições positivas, na esteira da alta do petróleo no exterior. O contrato futuro do índice com vencimento mais curto , em 14 de outubro, subia 0,16%.

item.title: Croatian court allows extradition of Nord Stream blast suspect to Germany, media reports
item.description: A Croatian court has ruled that a Ukrainian man suspected of being involved in the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline blasts can be extradited to Germany, Ukraine's Suspilne news portal reported on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Croatian court has ruled that [USN:L6N44H0T9 TEXT:"a Ukrainian man"] suspected of being involved in the 2022 [USN:L8N3UD0YM TEXT:"Nord Stream pipeline blasts"] can be extradited to Germany, Ukraine's Suspilne news portal reported on Thursday. German prosecutors have said the man — identified as Vladimir Z. — was a scuba diver who was part of a group behind the blasts, which followed Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine earlier that year. The explosions — described by Russia and Western countries as sabotage — damaged the Nord Stream 1 pipeline, a vital route for Russian gas exports to Europe, as well as the Nord Stream 2 branch, which had yet to enter service. Vladimir Z.'s lawyer, Mykola Katerynchuk, dismissed the court ruling, made on Friday last week, as biased and political and said there would be an appeal, according to the Suspilne report.
